title: Veal Orloff
description:
It was when we lived in Manhattan in the 1970’s that we started eating and cooking with more zest. This was also near the beginning of the “food revolution” in America.
Most enlightening for us were the NY Times articles (and later books) entitled “60-Minute Gourmet,” by Pierre Franey. These were great – varied, doable, and tasty – and still some of our favorite recipes.
This Veal Orloff is a good example of a dish based on a “once-in-a-life-time” meal, but done “without all of the theatrics” of the original.
START TO FINISH: 60 MIN
Veal Orloff
Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Sprinkle the chops with salt and pepper to taste and set aside.
Chop the mushrooms, producing about 1½ cups. Chop the onions. Squeeze the lemon.
Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in a small skillet. Add the onion and cook, stirring, until wilted.
Add the mushrooms and sprinkle with lemon juice. Cook, stirring, until the mush-rooms become fairly dry. Add salt and pepper to taste, stir, and set aside.
Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a saucepan and add the flour. Cook, stirring briefly, without browning. (This is the beginning of making a Béchamel Sauce.)
ingredients: 4 veal chops, about ¾ pounds each (loin chops shown here, but could be rib chops)
½ pound fresh mushrooms, finely chopped
2 tablespoons grated Gruyere or Swiss Cheese
directions: Add the milk, stirring rapidly with a whisk. When blended and smooth, add the cream, stirring. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Remove from the heat and add the cheese. Stir to blend and set aside (the is basicaly a Mornay Sauce).

Melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter in a large, heavy skillet. Add the chops and cook 1-2 minutes on one side or until nicely browned. Turn and cook about 1-2 minutes on the other side until equally well browned.
Transfer chops to a baking dish. Spoon equal portions of the mushroom mixture over each chop. Smooth it over.

Pour the fat from the skillet in which the chops cooked. Add the wine, stirring to dissolve the brown particles that cling to the bottom and sides of the skillet. Pour the pan sauce into the dish for baking the chops.
Spoon equal portions of the sauce around and over each chop.
Place the chops in the oven and bake 5-6 minutes. Run the dish briefly under the broiler at the end of the time until it is nicely browned.
